review_locator: PMCID:PMC3838198, The IL-10/STAT3-mediated anti-inflammatory response; PMCID:PMC4629104, New Frontiers for the NFIL3 bZIP Transcription Factor in Cancer, Metabolism and Beyond
primary_title: A Distal Enhancer in Il12b Is the Target of Transcriptional Repression by the STAT3 Pathway and Requires the Basic Leucine Zipper (B-ZIP) Protein NFIL3
decision_basis: The reviews identify NFIL3 as an IL-10/STAT3-associated suppressor of IL12B; the cited primary demonstrates NFIL3 binding to a distal Il12b enhancer, enhancer-reporter repression, Nfil3-deficient macrophage effects and impaired IL-10-mediated suppression of IL-12p40.
limitations_preserved: Direct NFIL3 distal-enhancer repression supports a bounded macrophage Il12b gene edge; preserve IL-10/LPS, enhancer and partial-repression semantics, and do not infer IL-12 protein secretion, receptor signaling, SCI or terminal-TF effects automatically.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3838198, The IL-10/STAT3-mediated anti-inflammatory response; PMCID:PMC4650320, Genomic analysis of LPS-stimulated myeloid cells identifies a common pro-inflammatory response but divergent IL-10 anti-inflammatory responses
primary_title: A Distal Enhancer in Il12b Is the Target of Transcriptional Repression by the STAT3 Pathway and Requires the Basic Leucine Zipper (B-ZIP) Protein NFIL3
decision_basis: The reviews identify Nfil3 as a STAT3-associated IL-10 response gene; the cited primary shows LPS- or IL-10-associated Nfil3 induction is lost in Stat3-deficient macrophages and restored in the IL-10 pathway context, supporting a STAT3-to-Nfil3 gene induction bridge without proving direct STAT3 promoter occupancy.
limitations_preserved: STAT3-dependent Nfil3 induction is supported at the gene-regulation level but is not direct promoter-binding evidence; preserve the IL-10/autocrine context and do not infer NFIL3 protein abundance, IL-12 suppression outside the measured relay, SCI or terminal-TF effects automatically.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC10243866, The comprehensive role of apoptosis inhibitor of macrophage (AIM) in pathological conditions; PMCID:PMC10110879, Advances in the role of STAT3 in macrophage polarization
primary_title: Apoptosis inhibitor of macrophage (AIM) contributes to IL-10-induced anti-inflammatory response through inhibition of inflammasome activation
decision_basis: The reviews identify AIM/CD5L as an IL-10/STAT3-regulated macrophage gene; the cited primary demonstrates IL-10-induced STAT3 binding at AIM promoter regions, dose-dependent AIM promoter activation and STAT3-dependent AIM expression in macrophages.
limitations_preserved: Direct promoter binding and reporter activation support a bounded STAT3-to-AIM/CD5L gene edge; preserve IL-10/macrophage context and distinguish CD5L transcript from AIM protein and extracellular function, with no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC4074809, Lipocalin 2 in macrophages; PMCID:PMC4650320, Genomic analysis of LPS-stimulated myeloid cells identifies a common pro-inflammatory response but divergent IL-10 anti-inflammatory responses
primary_title: Interleukin-10-Induced Neutrophil Gelatinase-Associated Lipocalin Production in Macrophages with Consequences for Tumor Growth
decision_basis: The reviews identify LCN2/NGAL as an IL-10-responsive STAT3 and C/EBPbeta target; the cited primary shows IL-10-dependent recruitment of both factors to the human NGAL promoter, mutation/decoy sensitivity of both sites, ChIP-Western association and reduced NGAL mRNA after either factor is blocked.
limitations_preserved: Promote the cooperative promoter-factor gene edge, not a definitive direct STAT3-CEBPB physical complex; preserve human macrophage/IL-10 context and do not infer LCN2 secretion, receptor action, SCI or terminal-TF effects automatically.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7608745, The alternative macrophage relay: STAT6 passes the baton to EGR2; PMCID:PMC10524119, Epigenomic regulation of macrophage polarization: where do the nuclear receptors belong?
primary_title: The transcription factor EGR2 is the molecular linchpin connecting STAT6 activation to the late, stable epigenomic program of alternative macrophage polarization
decision_basis: The reviews identify PPARG as a downstream transcription-factor target in the IL-4/STAT6/EGR2 macrophage relay; the cited primary demonstrates EGR2 occupancy at Pparg regulatory regions, Egr2-dependent Pparg induction and protein expression, and downstream ligand-responsive PPARgamma gene programs.
limitations_preserved: EGR2 occupancy plus Egr2-dependent Pparg induction supports a bounded macrophage gene bridge downstream of STAT6; preserve temporal STAT6/EGR2 separation and do not infer PPARgamma activity, lipid-ligand signaling, SCI or terminal-TF effects automatically.
